_about: Where a ship picture's engines are, when ThrusterFx's finder (the rearmost pixels, ThrusterFx.for_sprite) gets it wrong. Keyed by the picture's file name without .png; coordinates in that picture's own pixels (the full-size file; a _half picture halves them). Each engine is a column x and rows y0..y1: every row finds the hull's back edge from x (forward through plating to the first open pixel, or back through open space to the plating) and the flame starts on that edge. An empty list is a ship with no flame at all. Hand-placed Oct 13 off Jon's gallery verdicts; read each picture before adding one.

ship_asteroidtow.why: the tug's own engine; the rock it tows is the rearmost thing in the picture

ship_bigdish.why: the lit tail engine only; the dish's rim reaches further back

ship_scoop.why: the drive pod under the hull; the scoop's prong tips reach further back

hulk_honeycomb.why: the centre tail engine, its whole face: Jon found the 4-row flame too small; the fins either side are fins

hulk_rs_net.why: the hull's own stern between the net's fins

lancer_solarsail.why: the hull's rounded stern between the sails, not the sail tips

cutter_swarm.why: the whole flat stern plate; the finder took the antenna rod's tip

ship_cl_stack.why: bottom thruster pod; the pipe loop behind is not an engine

ship_courier2.why: the lower thruster block, not the tail wing

ship_fm_domes.why: the thruster cylinder on top, not the back of the last dome

ship_mkt_slung.why: top thruster pod at the back
bottom thruster pod at the back

ship_orbitarms.why: the drive collar at the end of the spine, above the arm's rod
the drive collar, below the rod; the spheres behind are the orbit arms' weights, not engines
